NKE.rationale: NKE presents a rare case of near-full alignment across all three pillars in the negative direction. Pillar 1 (fundamentals): Earnings have collapsed — Q3 FY2026 EPS of $0.35 is down 35% YoY and represents a continued sequential slide from $0.78 (Q2 FY2024) through $0.54, $0.49, $0.53, and now $0.35. Operating margin has compressed to 5.8% from 7.5% YoY and 11.5% two quarters prior. Net margin is 4.6% versus 7.0% a year ago. Cash generation has deteriorated sharply: OCF of $430M is down 76% YoY from $1.79B. Revenue is essentially flat at $11.28B. The trajectory is unambiguously negative with no stabilization visible. Pillar 2 (valuation): At a P/E of 30.3x with a 3.3% earnings yield — below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.45% — the stock is expensive relative to its own history (was 20.6x a year ago when margins were double today's levels). The market is pricing a recovery that the data does not yet support. P/B at 4.8x is at the trough of its range, but this reflects price decline, not value creation. Pillar 3 (near-term catalyst): The next earnings release (June 30, 2026) is a potential catalyst, but multiple sell-side analysts have recently downgraded or cut targets (RBC to $50, JPMorgan to Underweight with $40 PT), consensus FY2026 EPS is ~$1.49 (down 31% YoY), and turnaround benefits are not expected until FY2027. The near-term catalyst skews negative — the risk of further disappointment in the upcoming print is elevated given China weakness (~30% decline since 2021), ~$1B tariff headwind, and competitive share loss to On/Hoka/Adidas. The franchise quality is real (27% global share, Jordan $7.27B revenue, 24 consecutive dividend increases), but a world-class brand with deteriorating execution, collapsing margins, and an expensive multiple is not an attractive investment at this juncture.
